Results:
- Both sides pre-agree on baud rate + frame format
Hence:
- Wrong timing = gibberish / framing errors

No negotiation / discovery
Results:
- UART does not announce voltage, baud, role, or capabilities
Hence:
- Settings must be known beforehand

div.div:
Voltage + GND reference
Results:
- Both sides need compatible voltage levels
- Both sides need shared reference for high/low
Hence:
- Crossing power domains may need level shifters or isolation

div.div:
Distance / capacitance / noise
Results:
- Longer wires distort edges and pick up noise
- Higher baud rate makes this worse
Hence:
- For long/noisy links, use electrical translators like RS-485/RS-422
- RS-485/RS-422 converts single-ended UART TX/RX into a differential pair and back
- Or use USB for the long distance, and UART only short and local

div.div:
Buffering / flow control
UART sends a byte stream
Results:
- If receiver cannot keep up, data may be dropped
Hence:
- RTS/CTS or software handling may be needed

Common formats:
- 115200 8N1 = baud rate 115200, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit
- 7E1 = 7 data bits, even parity, 1 stop bit
- 8O1 = 8 data bits, odd parity, 1 stop bit
- 8N2 = 8 data buts, no parity, 2 stop bits
